verdict.rationale: LM Studio documents llmster as a headless daemon with no desktop app required, built for servers, cloud instances and CI. It is backed by a scriptable `lms` CLI (server start/stop, load, get) and a headless Local LLM Service with on-demand model loading. A community user confirms the headless flow works from real tools, though an older thread noted the full Electron UI was once required. Missing for 10: documented end-to-end CI recipes (non-interactive install, exit codes, pipeline examples) and hands-on reports of use in CI specifically.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: llmster is the headless version of LM Studio, no desktop app required. It's ideal for servers, CI environments, or any machine where you don't need a GUI.
llmster is LM Studio's headless daemon for servers, cloud instances, and CI.

Headless mode, or "Local LLM Service", enables you to leverage LM Studio's technology (completions, chat completions, embedding, structured outputs via `llama.cpp` or `Apple MLX`) as local server powering your app.

lms server start
lms server stop
The headless LM Studio flow is especially nice because it makes local inference usable from real tools instead of as a demo.
